fields.features_heading: Inside Each Comparison Page Emergent Builds
fields.features_subheading: Each page sets your product beside a named rival with a source under every claim, then records the visitors who pick you.
fields.feature_1:
A table built from your notes

Paste what you know about your product and each rival, one row per feature or price. Emergent builds the comparison table from those notes and changes any row when you prompt it.
fields.feature_2:
A source link under each rival cell

Each claim about a rival keeps the link it came from, such as the rival's pricing page. The app stores that URL with the date you checked it and shows the link under the cell.
fields.feature_3:
A reminder when a claim gets old

Set an age, such as 90 days, and the app flags each rival cell checked longer ago than that. The page owner gets the list by email or Slack, with the source link for every cell.
fields.feature_4:
Switchers saved with the tool they left

A switch form asks which tool the visitor uses now and when it renews. Each answer is a row in a database you own, and a rule you write sends big accounts to one named person.
fields.feature_5:
A new rival page from one prompt

Name a new rival and Emergent builds its page in the same layout, with its own table, sources, and form. Leads from all pages land in one table, tagged with the page they came from.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain first, your code later

Start on the free tier, which covers building and publishing. Custom domains are included and use credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository at any time.

fields.tab_content_1:
Six rival claims, each with its source

Pallisend sells invoicing to freelancers, and its Pallisend vs Kestrelby page compares the two on six rows. Each Kestrelby cell links to the page on Kestrelby's own site that the claim came from, and one row says plainly that Kestrelby has the mobile app. This month 412 visitors landed, and 57 started a trial.
fields.tab_content_2:
Big lists go by Slack to the migration lead

Plumcast's switching page is for Thistlebeck users. Its form asks for the list size and the renewal date. Lists over 50,000 contacts post to #migrations in Slack for Lunetta Wakely, the migration lead, and smaller lists get import steps by email. Beaconry Supply entered 62,000 contacts.
fields.tab_content_3:
Rival cells past 90 days go into Ansel's inbox

Grenwald compares its restaurant scheduling app with three rivals in one table. Each of the 24 rival cells is stored with its source and the date someone last checked it. A cell checked more than 90 days ago is flagged. This week 4 cells crossed that line, and Ansel Ninnis, who owns the page, got them by email.
fields.tab_content_4:
Payroll for 18 employees comes in $62 under

Coppervane prices payroll at $40 a month plus $6 per employee. Its comparison page has a calculator where a visitor types a headcount and the monthly bill from their current provider. A bakery owner entered 18 employees and $210, and the page showed $148, or $62 less each month. Each estimate is saved as a row.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Competitor Comparison Page
fields.howto_description: Follow seven steps to plan competitor comparison landing pages with fair, sourced claims, then build them on Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Start from the phrase a buyer types
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Name the rows before the columns
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Link each rival claim to the rival's page
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Give the rival its real wins
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the exact search, such as your name vs the rival's, or the rival's name plus alternative. A vs page and an alternatives page answer different questions. Give each one its own page, headline, and first paragraph.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pull the rows from sales calls and lost deals: the price at the buyer's team size, the feature they need this quarter, the time setup takes. Keep the table to six or eight rows so a buyer reads it to the end.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Point every rival cell at its origin on the rival's own site, a help center article or a public price list, and note the day you checked it. A reader who doubts a cell can open the source in one click.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put the rival's strengths in the table too, such as a mobile app you do not have. A page that concedes one row reads as fair, and a buyer who needs that feature leaves before a sales call that goes nowhere.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Put one next step under the table
fields.howto_step_5_des: Place a single button below the table: a trial, a demo, or a switch form. For switchers, ask when the current contract ends. The person who follows up can then time the call to the month before renewal.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Pick a recheck age for rival cells
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide how old a rival cell may get, such as 90 days, before someone checks it again. Rival prices and plans change without notice to you, and a stale cell is the first thing the rival's customers will point out.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Ship one rival, then the next
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the page for the rival that comes up first in lost deals and read its trial or demo count for a month. Then build the next rival's page with the same rows, and readers can compare your pages with each other too.

faq_plan.q: What are competitor comparison landing pages?
faq_plan.a: Competitor comparison landing pages are pages on your own site that compare your product with one named rival, row by row. They answer a search for one product against the other, or for an alternative to the rival, with a table and one next step, such as a trial.

faq_plan.q: How do I create competitor comparison landing pages?
faq_plan.a: Write down the search you want to answer, pick six to eight rows buyers decide on, and find the source for every rival claim. Then describe the page to Emergent's AI landing page builder. It builds the table and the form from your prompt, and each lead lands in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What should the table on competitor comparison landing pages include?
faq_plan.a: The table should hold the rows a buyer decides on, each side's answer in plain words, and a source link under every rival cell. Add the date each rival cell was checked. Drop rows where both products match, unless buyers expect to see them.

faq_plan.q: How do I learn which features to compare on competitor comparison landing pages?
faq_plan.a: Ask them. Send a five-question survey to recent customers and to deals you lost, asking which tools they looked at and which difference decided it. A training software company could borrow from learning and development survey questions to hear how its buyers rank features. Emergent builds the survey from a prompt, with no response caps.

faq_plan.q: Can competitor comparison landing pages name the rival brand they compare against?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The FTC's policy on comparative advertising encourages naming competitors, but requires clarity and, if necessary, disclosure to avoid deceiving the consumer. In practice, say what you compared and link the rival's own page for each claim. For anything beyond that, ask a lawyer.

faq_plan.q: How do I make competitor comparison landing pages work on a phone?
faq_plan.a: Keep two columns on a phone: your product and one rival, with the row label above each pair of answers. Pin the column names to the top of the screen as the reader scrolls. Put a third rival behind a switch at the top instead of a sideways scroll.

faq_plan.q: Which rival should I build competitor comparison landing pages against first?
faq_plan.a: Start with the rival your lost deals name first, because that page answers a question your buyers already ask. Check that people search the two names together before you write. A game studio can ask players which titles they also play with game survey questions, then compare against the one named first.

faq_plan.q: How often should competitor comparison landing pages be updated?
faq_plan.a: Recheck every rival cell on a fixed schedule, such as every 90 days, and again whenever a rival announces new pricing. Change the check date on the page each time. In an app Emergent builds, each check date sits in your own database, and the app can email the page owner when a cell passes its age.

faq_plan.q: Should competitor comparison landing pages show the rival's prices?
faq_plan.a: Show a rival's price only when the rival publishes it, and link the public page with the date you read it. If the rival quotes prices on request, say that instead of guessing a number. A price you estimated is a claim you cannot back up.

faq_plan.q: What do buyers want from competitor comparison landing pages?
faq_plan.a: Buyers on a comparison page already have a shortlist. They want the one difference that settles it, with proof they can open and check. To hear it from your own readers, send audience survey questions to your newsletter list before you write the rows.

plan.angle: The top 10 for competitor comparison landing pages is advice: agency and SaaS blog guides (TripleDart, Unkover, contadu), a Reddit thread asking how long vs pages take to build, a LinkedIn post on the mistakes, and Dribbble shots. None shows a built page with its table, the source behind each rival claim, and what happens to the visitors it wins. This page shows four built pages for four kinds of comparison (a head-to-head page, a switching page with a migration form, a three-rival table whose cells are rechecked, and a price calculator), each with what lands in the database. The FAQ covers the definition, building one, what a comparison table holds, naming a rival under the FTC's comparative advertising policy, mobile design, which rival goes first, keeping pages current, and admitting where a rival wins.
